metaDescription: Sebo bagged upright vacuums compared by sealed filtration, motor warranty, automatic height and brush obstruction shut-off for long-lived, repairable cleaning.
expertTake: The Sebo Automatic X4 is the best pick here because it adds automatic height adjustment, a 40 foot cord and a long motor warranty to the family's serviceable design. The Essential G5 is the value pick for a home that wants sealed filtration at the lowest tier. Skip the range if you want a light machine for stairs; these are heavy, built-to-last uprights.
introParagraphs: This maker builds bagged uprights that are closer to professional equipment than to a typical home machine: a metal-reinforced body, a sealed filtration path and parts that are designed to be replaced, not discarded. The design philosophy is to run for decades.

The cost of that approach is weight and price, and the benefit is a machine that holds its performance and can be repaired. The questions are how much automation you want, what warranty you need and whether the machine will be used for pets, large floors or mixed surfaces.

products.name: Sebo Automatic X4 9570AM, 7-year motor warranty, auto height
products.description:
The X4 is the machine that sells the brand: automatic height adjustment means the head sets itself for carpet and hard floor without a dial, a 40 foot cord covers a big room without changing outlets and three full-size tools ride on the body. The maker backs it with a 7-year motor warranty and a lifetime belt warranty, which is the strongest durability statement in this guide.

A low profile of about 5.5 inches reaches under furniture. Compared with the Essential G5 it adds automatic height and the longer warranty, while the G5 adds a few convenience features. The Dart offers a powered head for pets.

Upkeep is simple and cheap. Change the filter bag when it is about two thirds full, check the belt access cover, and keep a spare belt and filters with the machine. Because the belt is warrantied, you can swap it yourself in a couple of minutes, and the sealed filtration path means the bag does most of the work of keeping dust out of the air. Treat the cord with the respect a long cord deserves: wind it in loose loops on the hooks, check the strain relief at the body once a year and never let the head run over it, because a 40 foot cord is the most expensive part to replace and the most common casualty in a house where the vacuum is used daily. The 5.5 inch profile is only an advantage if you tilt the handle low when you go under a bed, so make a habit of that rather than pushing the head in at an angle that scrapes the frame.
products.bestFor: Homes that want a repairable upright with automatic height and a long warranty.
pros: Seven year motor warranty and lifetime belt warranty
cons: Costs more than typical home uprights

products.name: Sebo Essential G5 90407AM, 15 in path, sealed filtration
products.description:
The G5 is the family's pet upright: a 15 inch path, a tightly sealed hospital-grade filtration path, a soft start that eases the motor on, an instant-use wand and suction hose and a brush obstruction light with automatic shut-off. The brand calls it among the world's best pet vacuums, a marketing claim, but the sealed bag path and the obstruction light are real features.

It carries a low 5.5 inch profile and three on-board tools. Against the X4 it lacks automatic height, but costs less and brings the wide path.

Watch the obstruction light: when it comes on, switch off and clear the roll of hair or thread, which protects the belt. Replace the filter bag at two thirds full and the exhaust filter on schedule, and store the tools clipped to the body so that none goes missing. A sealed machine is only sealed when the bag door is closed properly, so listen for the click each time and never run it with the bag compartment ajar, even for a quick pickup. The soft start is a gentle feature that spares the motor and the circuit, but it also means the machine takes a second to reach full speed, so wait for the roll to spin before you push, and the first inch of each stroke will not be left uncleaned. Finally, learn what the obstruction light looks like when it first comes on, because it is the earliest warning that a long strand of hair is winding on the roll.
products.bestFor: Pet households that want sealed filtration and a wide path.
pros: Brush obstruction light with automatic shut-off

products.name: Sebo Dart 9855AM, ET-1 powerhead, 7-year motor warranty

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Stops the brush roller and alerts you

products.description:
The Dart is sold with the ET-1 powerhead, a motorized head that the maker describes as engineered for pets and carpet. A built-in safety system stops the brush roller and alerts you when the roll is blocked, which prevents a burnt belt. A 7-year motor warranty backs it.

Compared with the X4 it is aimed at pet households, while the X4 leads on the lifetime belt warranty and the 40 foot cord. The powerhead makes the Dart a particularly good partner for stairs and upholstery.

Check the alert whenever it sounds, empty the bag at two thirds full and keep the powerhead's hose free of kinks. The powerhead is a motorized part, so keep its contacts clean and avoid pulling it by the hose. The Dart suits a house with several flights of stairs because the powerhead does the agitation that a plain nozzle cannot, but the powerhead has its own small roll that collects hair, so slide the cover off every few weeks and clear it with a seam ripper, and check the electrical contacts where the powerhead plugs into the hose for dust, since a dirty contact makes the powerhead cut out and look faulty. Keep a spare belt for the powerhead as well as for the main head.
products.bestFor: Pet homes with stairs that want a powered tool and a long warranty.
pros: ET-1 powerhead for pets and carpet
Safety system stops a blocked roll

products.name: Sebo Essential G4 90406AM, low 5.5 in profile

specList.label: Profile
specList.value: 5.5 inch height to go under furniture

products.description:
The G4 is the entry model of the Essential line, and its listing makes one clear point: a 5.5 inch height profile that lets it slide under furniture. It is a plainer machine than the G5, with fewer convenience features.

The listing gives little else, so treat it as the baseline of the brand: a bagged upright with a low profile and the same design philosophy as the others. If you want automatic height or a powerhead, step up.

Change the filter bag early, check the belt and keep spare filters. If the seller cannot list the filtration and the tool kit, ask before buying. Because the listing is sparse, compare the model number with the maker's own range page, and make sure the bag and filter you plan to buy are the ones listed for this exact unit, since the family uses several bag styles and a wrong one leaves a gap at the intake. Buy a spare belt and two bags with the machine, and register the product if the maker offers a warranty registration, which usually takes a few minutes and avoids an argument later.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a Sebo at the lowest tier with a low profile.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The X4 and Dart list a 7-year motor warranty, and the X4 adds a lifetime belt warranty. A warranty is the clearest signal of intended lifespan. Read the terms and keep the receipt, because a warranty covers the motor under normal household use and typically excludes belts and bags on the usual wear schedule, and a claim made years later is far easier when the receipt, the serial number and the registration are in one folder.

The X4 adjusts its head height automatically, so it handles carpet and hard floor without a dial. Manual models rely on you remembering. Automatic height is worth the price in a mixed home, particularly when several people share the machine, since the one person who sets the height wrong is the one who leaves a streak on the rug or scatters crumbs across the kitchen, and an automatic head removes that variable altogether.

The G5 lists a tightly sealed hospital-grade filtration path. A sealed bagged upright keeps fine dust out of the air. Check the seal on the bag door, and replace the exhaust filter on the maker's schedule, because the filter holds the finest particles and a spent filter lets them through, and note that the sealed path is only as good as the bag you fit, so buy genuine bags for the exact model number rather than a loosely fitting substitute.

The G5 has an obstruction light with automatic shut-off, and the Dart a safety system that stops the roll. Hair and thread jams are the leading cause of burnt belts. This feature protects the machine, but only if you respond to it, so when the light comes on or the alert sounds, switch off, unplug and clear the roll at once, rather than continuing to the end of the room, because the belt heats in seconds when the roll is blocked and a stretched or burnt belt is the typical result of ignoring the warning.

These machines are heavy, built for durability. Carrying one up a flight is a chore. Plan to keep it on one floor or buy a second light machine, and if you must carry it, lift it by the handle with the body tilted against your leg and the cord held in the other hand, since the weight is concentrated in the motor housing and swinging it away from the body strains the wrist and the handle joint.

The X4 has a 40 foot cord and the G5 a 15 inch path. A long cord and a wide path mean fewer outlet changes and fewer passes. They also add weight, and a wide path is harder to steer around chair legs, so a household with a lot of furniture may finish faster with the narrower head, while an open-plan home with large rugs benefits from the wider path and the longer cord.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored the 7-year motor warranty on the X4 and Dart, and the lifetime belt warranty on the X4, because the belt is the wear part that most often stops a machine and a warranty on it shows that the maker expects the machine to be maintained and used for many years.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for sealed paths and for any statement about the bag door and the exhaust filter. The G5 lists a tightly sealed hospital-grade path, and we treated the other models as sharing the brand's bagged approach without a separate claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Protection features
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted obstruction lights and safety stops.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted weight and the low profile, since a machine that cannot get under a bed or a sofa leaves dust where it collects, and we also noted that the wide path and the long cord trade some maneuverability for fewer passes and fewer outlet changes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest claim reading
howWeEvaluated.description: We treated marketing phrases as claims.

cards.label: Automatic
cards.text: The X4 sets its own height, so it suits mixed homes and users who forget settings.

cards.text: The G4 and G5 rely on you. They cost less but need attention.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A motor warranty, a lifetime belt warranty and replaceable parts. Keep spares of the belt, the bag and the filter, and register the product so that the warranty is easy to claim.

cards.text: The X4 has a 7-year motor warranty and a lifetime belt warranty, and the Dart a 7-year motor warranty.

cards.text: You want a machine to last decades. The X4 or Dart pay back in repairability.

maintenance.why: A packed bag collapses airflow and strains the motor. Change it when it is about two thirds full, fit only the style listed for your model and close the bag door until it clicks, because a gap breaks the sealed path.

A worn belt stops the roll. The X4 belt is warrantied, and on the others a belt is a cheap part that takes a couple of minutes to change through the access cover, so replace it at the first sign of slipping and keep a spare in the closet with the manual.

Hair and thread block the roll and heat the belt. Switch off and unplug, cut the strands along the roll with scissors or a seam ripper and spin it by hand to confirm that it turns freely before you start again.
A loaded filter strains the motor and lets fine dust pass. Follow the maker's interval, fit only the specified filter and keep a spare so that the vacuum is never run without one.
A blocked hose looks like a weak motor. Pet hair and a stray sock can plug the bend, so detach the hose and look through it against a light, and push a broom handle through gently if it is blocked.

faq.a: They are built like professional equipment with repairable parts and long warranties. The price reflects a heavier body, a sealed bagged path and a design meant to last decades, and over a long life the cost per year can be lower than a cheaper machine replaced every few years.

Yes, all of them. Bags contain dust and are a recurring cost, but they are also the reason the machines stay clean inside and keep their suction, so budget for a year of bags when you compare the running cost with a bagless machine.

Yes. They are built to last, so carrying one up stairs is a chore, and a household with several flights should consider a second light machine for the upper floors while the Sebo lives on the main level where its wide path and long cord are most useful.

faq.q: What does the obstruction light do?
faq.a: It warns when the roll is blocked and can shut it off, protecting the belt. A blocked roll heats the belt within seconds, so the warning is one of the most useful features on the machine, provided you stop and clear the roll when it appears rather than finishing the room first.

A 7-year motor warranty is a strong signal that the maker expects the machine to run for years. Read the terms, keep the receipt and register the product, and remember that belts and bags are wear parts that you will buy regardless of the warranty.

faq.q: Which Sebo is best for pets?
faq.a: The Essential G5 or the Dart, depending on whether you want a wide path or a powerhead. The G5 suits large rooms of carpet and bare floor with shedding pets, and the Dart suits a home where the stairs and the sofa carry as much fur as the floor, so choose by where the hair actually lands.
